skill.displayName: Pet Adaptive Drying Temperature Recommendation | 宠物烘干温度自适应推荐

version.changelog:
- User identity handling is now fully automatic and internal; users are no longer prompted to provide or see any open-id or identity information.
- Historical report queries and all analysis operations no longer expose or require manual input of user identifiers.
- Updated documentation and usage instructions to reflect the removal of open-id parameters from user-facing workflows and command examples.
- Minor code and config adjustments to support seamless internal identity management.

llm.summary: The skill is mostly a server-backed pet media analysis tool, but it silently creates/reuses identity records, stores tokens locally, and can query cloud report history, so users should review its privacy impact before installing.

dimensions.detail: Uploading pet images/videos to a backend and returning drying recommendations fits the stated purpose, and history listing is documented, but automatic identity creation, token handling, and cloud history access materially broaden the privacy surface.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill tells the agent to auto-save uploaded media, call cloud APIs, and auto-trigger history queries from keywords; those actions are disclosed in the skill text but are broad for a media-analysis workflow without an explicit user consent step.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install-time shell script or persistence installer; dependencies are ordinary Python libraries. A static finding flagged a raw LAN IP in a dev config, but the active prod config points to public lifeemergence.com endpoints.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill reads local media files, can forward URLs for server-side fetching, reads workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt if present, creates a local data directory/database, and makes outbound requests; most are related to the service, but the implicit identity file use is under-scoped.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: It creates a local SQLite database and stores user identity plus token/open_token values after silent login or registration. There is no evidence of background execution, privilege escalation, destructive local behavior, or obfuscation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with pet media and report metadata being sent to the Life Emergence/SMYX backend, a local identity and token database being created, and cloud report history being retrievable through the skill. Avoid sharing media that includes people, home interiors, location clues, or other private content unless that processing is acceptable.
llm.findings:
[AST7] expected: The dynamic DAO filters are a generic local ORM helper issue, not evidence of code execution or malicious behavior in the reviewed workflow; this is a hardening concern only.
[LP3] unexpected: Network, file read/write, and command invocation are central to the skill, but the artifact lacks a clear permissions boundary or consent model for those capabilities.
[SDI-1] expected: Generic analysis and report-listing helpers are partly shared infrastructure and the entrypoint sets the pet-drying scene code, but report history access still increases data exposure beyond one-shot analysis.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Silent default identity generation, reading a local identity file, server-side login/registration, and local token persistence are not sufficiently justified by the pet drying recommendation purpose.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Auto-triggering on pet media can cause local saving and external processing before a user has clearly requested that handling.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The skill discloses local uploads and API use in the instructions, but does not clearly disclose retention, third-party processing, or credential/token storage to the end user.
[E1] unexpected: The code posts openId/mobile/source to an external login endpoint for silent account creation or reuse; that is a real outbound identity flow and is the main reason for Review rather than benign.
[suspicious.install_untrusted_source] unexpected: The raw-IP endpoint appears in an inactive dev config while prod config uses public service URLs, so this does not by itself drive the verdict but remains worth publisher cleanup.
